question: A 57-year-old man with rheumatoid arthritis undergoes regular treatment with corticosteroids. It is under study for presenting a picture of pain in the epigastrium, with occasional nausea and decreased appetite. In the analysis it presents: Hb 15 g / dL, Fe 55 ug / dL, PCR 3 mg / dL, ESR 42 mm at the first hour. Fibrogastroscopy: hiatus hernia of 3 cm and an ulcer at the level of the antrum, excavated, of 1 cm, with high and regular borders and with confluence of folds, which is biopsied. The histological study shows signs of acute inflammation and intestinal metaplasia. Normal abdominal CT What attitude, of those mentioned below, do you consider to be the most appropriate for the treatment of this patient?

options.opb: Treatment with proton pump inhibitors and a control gastroscopy with biopsy at 8 weeks.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient has rheumatoid arthritis" -> "Undergoes regular corticosteroid treatment" -> "Corticosteroids can cause gastric mucosal damage" -> "Patient presents with epigastric pain and ulcer" -> "Fibrogastroscopy shows ulcer with acute inflammation" -> "Histology shows intestinal metaplasia" -> "Indicates possible malignancy risk" -> "Eradicating treatment of Helicobacter pylori may reduce ulcer recurrence" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has a 1 cm ulcer in the antrum" -> "Ulcer is excavated with high and regular borders" -> "Histological signs of acute inflammation present" -> "Intestinal metaplasia suggests chronic irritation" -> "Proton pump inhibitors can promote healing of gastric ulcers" -> "Control gastroscopy with biopsy at 8 weeks is standard practice" -> "Monitoring for malignancy is essential" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Corticosteroids are being used" -> "Corticosteroids can exacerbate gastric ulcers" -> "Suspending corticosteroids may improve ulcer healing" -> "However, it may worsen rheumatoid arthritis symptoms" -> "Balancing ulcer treatment and arthritis management is crucial" -> "Unclear if suspension alone is sufficient" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Patient has a hiatus hernia" -> "Surgical treatment may be indicated for large hernias" -> "Billroth I is a surgical option for gastric ulcers" -> "However, it is invasive and not first-line for ulcers" -> "Less likely to be the most appropriate treatment" -> 60%
analysis: The patient presents with an antral ulcer and signs of acute inflammation, which raises concern for potential malignancy given the intestinal metaplasia observed in the biopsy. The most appropriate initial management for peptic ulcers, especially in the context of potential malignancy, is to initiate treatment with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) to promote healing and reduce gastric acid secretion. A follow-up gastroscopy with biopsy at 8 weeks is essential to reassess the ulcer and rule out malignancy. Eradicating Helicobacter pylori is also important but is secondary to the immediate need for acid suppression and monitoring. Therefore, the best option is to treat with PPIs and plan for follow-up endoscopy.
